headline: High: shared filesystem/MCP and overlapping writes make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write repo files and use MCP; TREK also exposes files, WebSocket, and MCP. That creates a plausible shared-channel injection path where content from one agent can be treated as instructions by the other. The pair is not documented as isolated, so uncertainty stays above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or MCP server, injected instructions can cross from one to the other.
IF TREK renders or forwards Gemini-generated text without provenance checks, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Disable shared MCP servers unless explicitly needed.
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent text transfers.
Require manual review before executing instructions from the other agent.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, shell environment, and broad network egress; TREK handles reservations, documents, photos, API keys, and MFA secrets. If they share a workspace or account context, sensitive travel data can flow into Gemini's third-party backend or TREK logs/outputs without a default barrier. The pairwise leakage path is plausible and high impact.
conditions: IF the same directory contains TREK secrets or reservations and Gemini CLI reads it, those contents can be transmitted off-host.
IF TREK logs or exports Gemini-produced text containing secrets, the data persists in ./data/logs/trek.log or uploads.
mitigations: Keep TREK data in a separate directory from Gemini work.
Redact secrets before Gemini reads any TREK artifacts.
Disable or restrict Gemini network egress for sensitive sessions.
Rotate any exposed API keys or MFA secrets after shared-session use.
Review TREK logs for accidental secret capture.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; TREK is collaborative and stores mutable state in travel.db, uploads, and logs. With overlapping write surfaces and no stated locking between the pair, concurrent edits can corrupt files or git state. The default shared-state model makes conflict likely rather than exceptional.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repo or data directory, last-writer-wins corruption can occur.
IF Gemini commits while TREK updates shared files, git state can diverge without locks.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate writable directory.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared state.
Use file locks around travel.db and git operations.
Snapshot the workspace before concurrent runs.
Move shared mutable data behind an API with locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can generate code, shell commands, and file edits; TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in and can act on documents, reservations, and user accounts. If TREK consumes Gemini output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into incorrect travel actions. The pathway exists, but direct autonomous action is not fully evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF TREK ingests Gemini-produced plans or commands without verification, downstream actions can be wrong.
IF Gemini fabricates a reservation detail that TREK stores or displays, the error propagates to users.
mitigations: Require human approval before TREK acts on Gemini output.
Add validation against source reservations and documents.
Mark Gemini outputs as untrusted until checked.
Use structured schemas for handoff data.
Log and diff all AI-generated changes before publish.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles reservations, documents, photos, country visit history, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while Gemini CLI can send file contents to Google-hosted inference via broad network egress. That creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated travel or identity data is placed into Gemini sessions. The other agent is cited because the risk is the cross-agent flow.
conditions: IF EU PII or sensitive travel documents are copied into Gemini CLI, they may leave the self-hosted TREK boundary.
IF TREK stores data subject to retention or residency rules and Gemini processes it externally, policy mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Gemini prompts.
Use a DPA-approved deployment for any external processing.
Separate residency-sensitive records from AI-assisted workflows.
Document retention and deletion handling for shared artifacts.
Restrict Gemini sessions to non-sensitive summaries.
